clue.text: Losing to drunk is a disgrace

indicators.note: losing says the word to is taken away from the word for drunk

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moralist's verdict that getting drunk and losing your grip is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain on one's reputation, a synonym for a disgrace.

clue.text: Monk upset about men lacking principle

indicators.note: about says the reversed monk goes round the men
in a down clue, upset turns the word for monk upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
OR, other ranks, stands for soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: A distressed monk complains about men who have no principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without any moral sense means having no principles at all, the meaning of amoral.

clue.text: See 18
Check on unemployed brother

indicators.note: on means the word for unemployed sits next to, after, the abbreviation for brother

parts.note: someone out of work is idle

explanation.surface: A sibling is told to keep tabs on his jobless brother.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the pieces in the opposite order to the answer; 'on' means the jobless word comes after the sibling's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to restrain or curb, as with a horse's headgear, so it means to check.

clue.text: Showing Fury freaking out — nastiest pre-fight

indicators.note: freaking out suggests going wild, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A boxer named Fury loses his cool and is at his nastiest before the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Fury suggests Tyson Fury the boxer, but here it is simply rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting feathers is a British idiom for being extremely angry, so it describes someone showing fury.

clue.text: Writer doesn't have a double

indicators.note: doesn't have says the letter a is dropped from the writer's name

parts.note: Mark Twain, the American author

explanation.surface: An author complains he has no double or stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is an exact match or counterpart, which is what a double is.

clue.text: See 5
See a lot of woman getting dressed

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A voyeuristic remark about seeing a lot of a woman's body while she gets dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See a lot of' reads as a phrase about seeing much flesh; in fact 'See' gives C and 'a lot of' trims LADY to LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, so it means wearing clothes.

clue.text: Sweet porn model gets embarrassed

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A glamour model blushes at the sweet nothings she hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a hard boiled sweet flavoured with lemon; sweet is British for a candy.

clue.text: Nasty bloke following with revolver

indicators.note: following puts the word for the nasty bloke after the letter for with

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A nasty man follows someone, carrying a handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun, but it is anything that turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel revolves on its axle, so it is literally a thing that revolves.

clue.text: Band beginning to hire and fire

parts.note: a torc is a metal band worn round the neck

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word hire

explanation.surface: A boss's habit with a music group: start by hiring them and then sack them.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set fire to it, so as verbs they are synonyms.

clue.text: Set off breaking into old school

indicators.note: breaking into says the school's name is placed inside the word for old

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: Burglars set off to break into an old school.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that is set off has been made to explode, which is what detonated means.

clue.text: Francis's responsibility under discussion — quite understand

indicators.note: under discussion means the words are spoken, so the spelling follows their sound

parts.note: quite means wholly, and to understand is to see

explanation.surface: A matter Pope Francis is debating, which he fully grasps.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis is Pope Francis, whose see (diocese) is Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the papal jurisdiction, the Pope's charge as Bishop of Rome.

clue.text: Trusted Henry's newspaper column

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an op-ed is an opinion piece printed opposite the editorial page

explanation.surface: A man named Henry's newspaper column was considered reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: To have hoped for something is to have trusted it would happen, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Vet belonging to cult keeps quiet

parts.note: to be in a group is to belong to it

indicators.note: keeps says the phrase holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult
P is the musical abbreviation piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A veterinarian in a cult stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' is the verb to check, not the animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully, which is to inspect it.

clue.text: "Isn't good", tattooed actor Christopher said in short

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, so the spelling follows their sound

parts.note: something that sucks, in slang, is bad; a tattooed person has been inked; Christopher Lee, the actor famous for Dracula

explanation.surface: Someone sums up briefly what a tattooed Christopher Lee thinks of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something succinctly means putting it briefly, which is what in short means.

clue.text: Taking humour to begin with — Screw has it and Tramp

indicators.note: taking means removing the first letter of humour from the word that follows

parts.note: a screw has a thread spiralling round it

indicators.note: to begin with means the first letter of humour

explanation.surface: A comic tale about humour and characters named Screw and Tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw and Tramp are both fellow Guardian setters, a nod by Vlad.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily, the same as to tread.

clue.text: Dishy fellow gets some crumpet, right?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sexy man gets a bit of crumpet, a British slang for an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'gets', which is only the link; the definition is 'Dishy fellow'. 'Dishy' points to good looks but means the man behind the laboratory dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Petri, German bacteriologist, gave his name to the Petri dish, so he is the fellow of the dish.

clue.text: Strange! Half two in empty dockyard — where is everybody?

indicators.note: strange signals that the following letters are made odd, i.e. rearranged
empty means the dockyard loses all but its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone at an eerily deserted dockyard at half past two asks where everyone has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves DD of dockyard. 'Half two' looks like a time; the words are just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom the world and his wife means a huge crowd, practically everybody.

clue.text: Gulls and other birds

definitions.meaning: to gull someone is to dupe them, and a pigeon is also a dupe or to dupe

explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is slang for a dupe, so pigeons gulls (tricks); they are also birds distinct from seagulls.

clue.text: Publicly criticises records

definitions.meaning: to criticise someone openly, humiliating them
to write something down or note it

explanation.surface: Someone who publicly attacks people keeps a log of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone down is belittling them; putting something down is writing it, as in recording it.

clue.text: Traveller's opening bag outside station

indicators.note: outside says the case goes round the opening letter

parts.note: a case is a bag, a suitcase

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of Traveller's

explanation.surface: A traveller opens a bag outside a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' looks like a railway stop; here it is social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Station means social position or standing, and a caste is a fixed social class.

clue.text: Extremely rich Scottish banker — it's annoying

parts.note: the Dee is a Scottish river, and a river has banks
a pest is something irritating

explanation.surface: A very wealthy banker from Scotland is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests finance but means a river; the Dee flows through Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep, like a voice or a colour, can mean rich, and deepest is the most intense degree.

clue.text: Son inclined to be awkward

parts.note: something tilted is set at an angle

explanation.surface: A boy who tends to be clumsy in social situations.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or behaviour is stiff and unnatural, which is awkward.

clue.text: Rule-breaking very accomplished but shameful

indicators.note: breaking means the letter for rule breaks into the words that follow

parts.note: so means very
to have done something is to have accomplished it

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules may be very skilful but still disgraceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sordid is morally squalid or dishonourable, the same as shameful.

clue.text: View of Boris Johnson? He's divisive

indicators.note: divisive means the pronoun splits the word for the politician

parts.note: Boris Johnson is a Conservative politician, a Tory
the he of the clue, with is as a link

explanation.surface: A political comment calling Boris Johnson a polarising figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an opinion or idea about something, which is what a view is.

clue.text: Food's tested! Hamburger's the …

parts.note: something proven has been tried and tested
a person from Hamburg speaks German, in which der is a word for the

explanation.surface: Fast-food test results run on into the next clue: the hamburger is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' suggests a burger; it means someone from Hamburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is an old word for food or provisions, originally animal fodder.

clue.text: Leading politician well-informed about cause of inflation

indicators.note: leading says the reversed word for well-informed comes in front of the politician
about means the word for well-informed is turned round

parts.note: to be up on something is to be knowledgeable
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A senior politician is knowledgeable about what causes rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading politician' looks like the Prime Minister, but 'Leading' just places the turned-round word first. 'inflation' means blowing something up, not prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump forces air into a tyre or balloon, blowing it up, so it causes inflation.

clue.text: See 19 across
… best — care for a trip to McDonald's?

indicators.note: to means the next letter is added on
a trip suggests being sent off on a wander, so the letters of care are rearranged

parts.note: McDonald's logo is the golden arches shaped like an M

explanation.surface: Continuing 24: the best idea is a trip to McDonald's.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 24's clue, so 'Hamburger's the … best' reads on.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as the best of the crop.

clue.text: Air base reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is written as it sounds

parts.note: base means low or contemptible, i.e. mean

explanation.surface: News about an air force base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air base' looks like a military site; 'Air' is the definition and 'base' the word sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their bearing or manner, the look or air they have.

clue.text: Fruit and honey available

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, a crossword convention
something on offer is on

explanation.surface: A greengrocer lists fruit and honey on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large fruit with a hard rind, such as a cantaloupe.

clue.text: Grew frustrated with trial — very clear to see

indicators.note: frustrated suggests things being thwarted and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone became visibly exasperated with a court trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something writ large is shown in a magnified, obvious form, so very clear to see.
